Issued at 300 AM EDT Sat Oct 24 2026

Today-Tonight...The Florida peninsula remains wedged between a 
strengthening surface high pressure across the eastern US and a 
stalled boundary draped across the northern Caribbean, maintaining
northeasterly winds locally. A tightening of the pressure 
gradient due to the strengthening high will lead to an increase in
winds today, with sustained speeds forecast to reach 15 to 20 mph
while gusts range between 25 to 35 mph. The strongest winds are 
anticipated along the coast, with conditions reaching Wind 
Advisory criteria along the Volusia and northern Brevard coastline
starting at 2 PM and expanding southward along the coast at 2 AM.
The persistent northeast winds are forecast to continue advecting
moisture from the Atlantic towards the coast, with a southward- 
moving mid-level trough providing some energy aloft to support 
onshore-moving showers today. While isolated activity has already 
begun across the local waters, coverage is anticipated to increase
this afternoon into the overnight hours, with the potential for 
some training bands to develop. As a result, WPC has outlooked the
east coast in a Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall today, 
with minor, localized flooding possible in some spots. 
Additionally, there is a low chance (20-30%) for storm activity to
develop, with isolated lightning strikes and occasional stronger 
wind gusts possible. As mentioned, activity is anticipated to 
persist into the overnight hours, and farther intrusion inland of 
showers will be possible. Temperatures remain near normal, with 
highs in the upper 70s to low 80s and lows in the mid 60s to low 
70s.

Hazardous to dangerous beach conditions are forecast along the 
east coast today as a result of the persistent northeast winds, 
high astronomical tides, and building seas. A high risk of rip 
currents is forecast along with rough surf. A High Surf Advisory 
has been issued for the Volusia and northern Brevard coasts 
starting at 11 AM, expanding southward to the rest of the east 
central Florida coast at 8 PM. Breaking waves of 6 to 10 feet are 
forecast, starting up north and expanding southward as seas 
continue to build overnight. The rough, pounding surf is also 
anticipated to result in beach erosion. A Coastal Flood Advisory 
is in effect along the entire east central Florida coastline for 
minor coastal flooding that is anticipated to peak during high 
tide, approximately between the hours of 5 to 7 AM/PM. Overall, 
conditions at the beach will be dangerous, and entering the ocean 
is not encouraged. Even heading to the beach could become 
hazardous, especially during periods of high tide. 

Sunday-Tuesday...The surface high across the eastern US will 
continue to strengthen and push southward through this weekend and
into early next week, while at the same time a broad area of low 
pressure gradually develops along a stalled boundary draped across
the northern Caribbean and meanders across the western Atlantic. 
The result will be a continued tightening of the pressure gradient
across the Florida peninsula, resulting in increasing wind speeds
locally. Northeast winds are forecast to reach 20 to 25 mph with 
gusts up to 40 mph starting on Sunday, with these windy and gusty 
conditions persisting into Monday and Tuesday. Wind Advisories 
will likely be needed areawide beginning on Sunday, with high 
confidence for advisories across portions if not most of east 
central Florida through the start of the work week. 

The persistent northeast flow will continue to advect moisture 
towards the Florida peninsula, with rain chances remaining high 
into Sunday (40-80%). Sunday looks to have the best chances for 
activity to push farther inland, and there is also a low chance 
(20-40%) for some storm development with activity as well. Any 
storms that do manage to develop may be capable of producing 
lightning strikes and strong wind gusts. Additionally, with the 
persistent northeast flow, training bands may develop across east 
central Florida, raising the risk for localized flooding. There is
currently a Slight Risk (2/4) of excessive rainfall across 
portions of the Treasure Coast, with a Marginal Risk (1/4) along 
northern portions of the coast. By Monday and Tuesday, rain 
chances are anticipated to decrease slightly to 30- 50%, with the 
highest coverage forecast along the coast primarily from the Cape 
southward. Minor flooding will remain a concern, with a Marginal 
Risk (1/4) of excessive rainfall continuing across portions of the
Treasure Coast into Monday and Tuesday. Temperatures are forecast
to remain seasonable in the upper 70s to low 80s during the 
afternoon hours, falling into the 60s to low 70s during the 
overnight hours.

With the persistent northeast flow, continued high astronomical 
tides, and high wave heights forecast, dangerous surf conditions 
are anticipated to continue along the east coast through this 
weekend and into early next week. Enter
